subject: Biology
why: Version 1 had 26 flat topics, several too broad and two joining topics the syllabus keeps apart. Version 2 moved to parent topics at the grain of the syllabus's numbered topics and subtopics at the grain of its sub-areas. Version 2.1 applied sixteen findings from placing all 46 settled 2025 questions into version 2 with a classifier that did not design it. Version 2.2 applies the coverage map of the WAEC, JAMB and scheme-of-work sources and a placement test of 80 UTME and 80 WAEC questions from 2015 to 2025: thirteen subtopics added where content had no home, covers lines widened where content plainly belonged, and sorting rules written on every border the two models split. No id was merged or removed. Every one of the 106 legacy database topics is folded in. Nothing in the database is changed by this file.

source.provenance_note: Third-party mirror, file dated 2015-09-24, author field awajis.com. The preamble is WAEC's own standard wording. Not fetched from a WAEC domain directly.
source.scope_rule: The syllabus states that Paper 1, the objective paper, is drawn from Section A. The real 2025 paper also tested Section B content (endocytosis in Q11, DNA in Q45 and Q46) and Section C content (plant life cycles in Q20, population measurement in Q35). So Section A is the spine, and Section B cell biology and Section C content are placed as subtopics, because that is where real questions land. Section B material that no Nigerian paper has been seen to test is left out until one does. Version 2.2 adds three homes on the same rule, for content real papers test beyond the syllabus wording: the nerve impulse (WAEC placement sample Q26), homeostasis as a concept (WAEC sample Q48), and red cell breakdown by the liver and spleen (UTME sample Q73). Section B items marked "Ghana only" in the WAEC syllabus (protein synthesis, identification keys, drug abuse, first aid, fish farming) are left out: Nigerian candidates do not sit them, and no Nigerian paper seen tests them.

how_to_use: Place a question by what a student must know to answer it, not by words in the stem. A question that mentions a leaf but tests osmosis goes under osmosis. Read the covers line before choosing; where two subtopics look close, the covers line says which one wins.

subtopics.name: Characteristics of living things
subtopics.covers: What separates living from non-living things: the characteristics of life.

subtopics.name: Classification and naming of organisms
subtopics.covers: Kingdoms and major groups, taxonomic ranks, binomial naming, which group an organism belongs to, and the distinguishing features of each group: bacteria as prokaryotes, algae, mosses, ferns, conifers and flowering plants, and the animal phyla. Sorting rule: a feature that places an organism in a group, including a prokaryote and eukaryote comparison, goes here; the structure, shapes and habitats of bacteria go to microorganisms.types; how an alga, moss or fern reproduces goes to reproduction.lower-organisms; ordering groups from primitive to advanced goes to evolution.trends; which group of organisms feeds in a stated way goes to animal-nutrition.modes.

subtopics.name: Differences between plants and animals
subtopics.covers: Features that distinguish plants from animals.

subtopics.name: Levels of organisation
subtopics.covers: Cell, tissue, organ and system levels, with examples of organisms at each, and the arrangement of the main organs in the body of a mammal. Sorting rule: where organs lie relative to one another goes here; the structure or work of one organ goes to that organ's subtopic.

subtopics.name: Complexity of organisation
subtopics.covers: How complexity increases from single cells to multicellular organisms, and its advantages. Sorting rule: ordering named groups of organisms from simple to advanced goes to evolution.trends, even when the stem speaks of complexity.

subtopics.name: Forms in which living cells exist
subtopics.covers: Single and free-living, colony, filament, and cells as part of an organism: Amoeba, Volvox, Spirogyra. Sorting rule: which form an organism takes, or its size and form, such as Spirogyra as a microscopic filament, goes here, even when the stem uses the word biomass. How a single cell moves or responds goes to cell.properties; how it feeds, excretes or reproduces goes to that process's subtopic; whether an organism such as Plasmodium lives as a parasite goes to associations.parasitism.

subtopics.name: Cell components and their functions
subtopics.covers: The cell theory and its history (Hooke, Dujardin, Schleiden, Schwann), then organelles and what each does: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, vacuole, cell wall, chloroplast, membranes. Sorting rule: how cilia, flagella or cytoplasmic streaming move a cell goes to cell.properties.

subtopics.name: Plant and animal cells compared
subtopics.covers: Structures found in one kind of cell and not the other.

subtopics.name: Movement and irritability in cells
subtopics.syllabus: A.I.6(f), SoW SS1 T1 W10, SoW SS2 T1 W7
subtopics.covers: How single cells and cells in organisms move and respond: cilia, flagella and pseudopodia, cytoplasmic streaming (cyclosis) as in Paramecium, and irritability, a cell's response to light, chemicals and touch. Sorting rule: how a single-celled organism moves or responds goes here, not under organisation.cell-forms or cell.components; growth responses of plants go to plant-response.tropisms.

subtopics.name: Cell division: mitosis and meiosis
subtopics.covers: Stages of mitosis and meiosis, the cell cycle, and where and why each division happens. Sorting rule: crossing over, and the number of chromosomes in a gamete, zygote or body cell worked out from haploid and diploid numbers, go here; chromosome structure, genes and DNA go to genetics.chromosomes; growth as a whole process of division, enlargement and differentiation goes to growth.growth.

subtopics.name: Diffusion
subtopics.covers: Movement of particles down a concentration gradient, and factors that change its rate.

subtopics.name: Osmosis and plasmolysis
subtopics.covers: Water movement across a membrane; hypotonic, isotonic and hypertonic solutions; turgidity, plasmolysis, crenation and haemolysis.

subtopics.name: Active transport
subtopics.covers: Movement against a concentration gradient using energy from respiration.

subtopics.name: Endocytosis and exocytosis
subtopics.covers: Bulk movement through the membrane: phagocytosis, pinocytosis and exocytosis. Added after 2025 Q11 tested it.

subtopics.name: Skeleton and support in animals
subtopics.covers: Types of skeleton, skeletal materials, bones of the vertebral column and limbs, functions of the skeleton. Sorting rule: naming a bone or a part of a bone, including a surface or process where a muscle attaches, goes here; how muscles move a joint goes to support.joints-movement.

subtopics.name: Joints, muscles and movement
subtopics.covers: Types of joint, antagonistic muscles, and how limbs move. Sorting rule: naming a bone or a part of a bone goes to support.animal-skeleton, even when the part is named for the muscle that attaches there.

subtopics.name: Supporting tissues in plants
subtopics.covers: Parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma and xylem as supporting tissues, and where each is found. Xylem and phloem as transport vessels go under transport.plants. Sorting rule: a tissue asked about for its supporting role goes here; the layers and arrangement of a root or stem go to support.plant-organs.

subtopics.name: Roots and stems: form and internal structure
subtopics.covers: Tap and fibrous roots, root hairs and the piliferous layer, kinds of stem, modified roots and stems including perennating organs, the internal layers of a root and a stem (cuticle, epidermis, cortex, endodermis, vascular bundles), and monocot and dicot plants compared across root, stem, leaf and seed. Real papers test it (UTME placement sample Q4 and Q62, WAEC sample Q5 and Q35). Sorting rule: a root or stem's form or layers, or a monocot and dicot comparison across organs, goes here; how water enters and moves through a plant goes to transport.plants; one leaf's own parts go to plant-nutrition.leaf; the parts of a seed alone go to growth.germination; a perennating organ used to propagate a plant goes to reproduction.asexual; a tissue's supporting role goes to support.plant-tissues.

subtopics.name: Need for transport
subtopics.covers: Why large organisms need a transport system: surface area to volume ratio and distance.

subtopics.name: Heart, blood vessels and circulation
subtopics.covers: Structure of the heart, arteries, veins and capillaries, and single and double circulation. Sorting rule: a named vessel of an organ, such as the renal artery or hepatic portal vein, and what it carries goes here; the organ's own structure and work go to its subtopic, such as excretion.kidney or excretion.liver.

subtopics.name: Blood and its functions
subtopics.covers: Composition of blood, what each component does, and the materials blood carries. Sorting rule: where old red cells are destroyed goes to excretion.liver; blood groups go to variation.applications or genetics.applications, not here.

subtopics.name: Transport in plants
subtopics.covers: Uptake and movement of water, xylem and phloem as vessels, translocation, and transpiration and the factors affecting it. Sorting rule: how water enters a root and moves through the plant goes here; where root hairs arise and a root's layers go to support.plant-organs.

subtopics.name: Aerobic and anaerobic respiration
subtopics.covers: Energy release in cells, aerobic against anaerobic respiration, products, fermentation and muscle fatigue.

subtopics.name: Respiratory surfaces and organs
subtopics.covers: Body surface, gills, lungs, tracheal system and leaves as surfaces for gaseous exchange, and their features.

subtopics.name: Mechanism of gaseous exchange
subtopics.covers: Breathing movements, how gases are exchanged at a surface, and the role of stomata.

subtopics.name: Excretory organs and waste products
subtopics.covers: Waste products of metabolism and the organs that remove them, in animals, plants and single cells: contractile vacuole, flame cell, nephridium, Malpighian tubule, kidney, stomata and lenticels, and plant excretory products (alkaloids, tannins, gums, resins, latex) with their economic uses. Sorting rule: the kidney's own structure and urine formation go to excretion.kidney.

subtopics.name: The kidney
subtopics.covers: Kidney structure, the nephron, how urine is formed, water balance, and kidney disease. Sorting rule: the renal artery and vein as vessels, and what they carry, go to transport.heart-circulation; the nephron and urine formation stay here; what homeostasis means goes to excretion.homeostasis.

subtopics.name: The liver
subtopics.covers: Liver functions, including making bile, deamination and storage, the breakdown of old red blood cells by the liver and spleen, and liver diseases such as cirrhosis and hepatitis. Sorting rule: where old red cells are destroyed goes here; red cell structure and work go to transport.blood; the hepatic portal vein as a vessel goes to transport.heart-circulation.

subtopics.name: The skin and temperature control
subtopics.covers: Skin structure and how it regulates body temperature. Sorting rule: what homeostasis means goes to excretion.homeostasis.

subtopics.name: Homeostasis
subtopics.syllabus: JAMB B.9(d), SoW SS3 T1 W1
subtopics.covers: The meaning of homeostasis, the internal environment, negative feedback, and which organs take part. Real papers test it (WAEC placement sample Q48). Sorting rule: what homeostasis is, and which organs share in it, goes here; how the kidney balances water goes to excretion.kidney, how the skin controls temperature to excretion.skin, and blood sugar control by insulin and glucagon to coordination.hormones.

subtopics.name: The central nervous system
subtopics.covers: Parts of the brain and their functions, and the spinal cord.

subtopics.name: Peripheral and autonomic nervous system
subtopics.covers: Somatic and autonomic systems, sympathetic and parasympathetic effects, and types of neurone. Sorting rule: how an impulse is started or crosses a synapse goes to coordination.impulse.

subtopics.name: The nerve impulse and synapse
subtopics.covers: How a neurone carries an impulse: stimulus threshold, the all-or-none law, the refractory period, and transmission across a synapse. Real papers test it (WAEC placement sample Q26). Sorting rule: how an impulse is started or passed on goes here; the kinds and structure of neurones go to coordination.pns; the path of an impulse round a reflex arc goes to coordination.reflex.

subtopics.name: Reflex and voluntary actions
subtopics.covers: The reflex arc, reflex against voluntary action, and conditioned reflexes.

subtopics.name: Animal hormones and endocrine glands
subtopics.covers: Endocrine glands, the hormones they make, their effects, and deficiency or excess.

subtopics.name: The eye
subtopics.covers: Structure of the eye, how it forms an image, accommodation, and eye defects and their correction.

subtopics.name: The ear
subtopics.covers: Structure of the ear, hearing and balance.

subtopics.name: Nose, tongue and skin
subtopics.covers: Smell, taste and touch receptors.

subtopics.name: Plant hormones
subtopics.covers: Auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins, abscisic acid and ethylene, their effects, and their influence on growth.

subtopics.name: Tropisms and nastic responses
subtopics.covers: Growth responses to light, gravity, water and touch, and nastic movements.

subtopics.name: Asexual reproduction
subtopics.covers: Fission, budding, spore formation and vegetative propagation. Sorting rule: using a corm, bulb, rhizome or tuber to propagate a plant goes here; identifying the organ by its structure goes to support.plant-organs; spores within the life cycle of a moss or fern go to reproduction.lower-organisms.

subtopics.name: Sexual reproduction in simple organisms and non-flowering plants
subtopics.covers: The general idea of sexual reproduction by the fusion of gametes, conjugation in Spirogyra and Paramecium, and the life cycles of mosses, ferns and conifers: alternation of generations, spores, and the need for water in fertilisation. Tested in UTME 2015 Q9 and 2018 Q10. Sorting rule: how an alga, moss, fern or conifer reproduces goes here, not under classification.kingdoms; spore formation as a kind of asexual reproduction goes to reproduction.asexual; human gametes and fertilisation go to reproduction.human; animal life histories go to growth.metamorphosis; annuals, biennials and perennials go to applied.plant-life-cycles.

subtopics.name: Human reproduction
subtopics.syllabus: reproduction (a)(i)-(v), SoW SS2 T1 W10, SoW SS3 T1 W8
subtopics.covers: Male and female reproductive systems, gametes, fertilisation, development of the embryo, birth control, family planning and reproductive health. Sorting rule: sexually transmitted infections as diseases go to microorganisms.disease.

subtopics.name: Reproduction in animals compared
subtopics.syllabus: reproduction (c), C courtship, C developing animal
subtopics.covers: Reproduction across animal groups, internal against external fertilisation, care of the young, yolk in eggs and the placenta as adaptations for the developing young, and courtship. Sorting rule: courtship and display behaviour, such as the lizard's gular fold or head nodding, goes here whether the answer is attracting a mate or warning off a rival; a body structure goes to adaptation.structural; territoriality, migration, hibernation and aestivation go to adaptation.behavioural.

subtopics.name: Flowers and pollination
subtopics.covers: Floral parts and their arrangement, types and agents of pollination, and placentation.

subtopics.name: Fertilisation, fruits and seed dispersal
subtopics.covers: Fertilisation in flowering plants, types and structure of fruits, and agents of dispersal. Sorting rule: how a seed forms after fertilisation goes here; the parts of a seed, including endospermous and non-endospermous seeds, go to growth.germination.

subtopics.name: Germination
subtopics.covers: Conditions for germination, epigeal and hypogeal germination, and seed structure, including endospermous and non-endospermous seeds. Sorting rule: the parts of a seed go here; fruit types, and how a seed forms after fertilisation, go to reproduction.fruits-seeds.

subtopics.name: Growth and its measurement
subtopics.covers: Growth as cell division, enlargement and differentiation, development, aspects of growth, regions of fastest growth, and how growth is measured. Sorting rule: the stages of mitosis go to cell.division.

subtopics.name: Metamorphosis and life histories
subtopics.covers: Complete and incomplete metamorphosis, nymphs and larvae, and life cycles of insects and other animals.

subtopics.name: Photosynthesis
subtopics.covers: The process, light and dark reactions, materials and conditions, limiting factors, and experimental evidence. Sorting rule: the process, its conditions and its products go here; which process adds or removes carbon (IV) oxide from the atmosphere goes to nutrient-cycles.carbon; energy change viewed across an ecosystem goes to energy-flow.energy.

subtopics.name: Leaf structure
subtopics.covers: External parts of a leaf (apex, margin, lamina, midrib, veins, petiole) and its internal tissues. The leaf is placed here as the organ of photosynthesis. Sorting rule: a comparison of monocot and dicot plants across several organs goes to support.plant-organs.

subtopics.name: Mineral nutrition
subtopics.covers: Macro and micro nutrients, their uses and deficiency symptoms, and the soil and air as sources. Sorting rule: carnivorous plants that trap insects for nitrogen go to animal-nutrition.modes.

subtopics.name: Food classes and balanced diet
subtopics.covers: Classes of food, their sources and uses, what each is built from (glucose, fructose and sucrose; starch; amino acids; fatty acids and glycerol), a balanced diet, and deficiency diseases. Sorting rule: what a food is built from goes here; what an enzyme breaks it into goes to animal-nutrition.enzymes; how to test for it goes to animal-nutrition.food-tests.

subtopics.name: Food tests
subtopics.covers: Tests for starch, sugars, protein and fat, and what a positive result looks like.

subtopics.name: Digestive enzymes
subtopics.covers: Each enzyme, what it acts on, what it produces, where it acts, and the conditions it needs. Sorting rule: a question about what an enzyme does, or where in the gut the digestion of a named food begins, goes here, even when it is answered by picking a region on a gut diagram; naming or describing the parts of the gut goes under alimentary.

subtopics.name: Modes of nutrition
subtopics.syllabus: A.II.2(e), A.I.6(a), C modes of nutrition
subtopics.covers: Autotrophic (photosynthetic and chemosynthetic), holozoic, parasitic, saprophytic and symbiotic nutrition, with single-celled examples such as Euglena and Amoeba, and carnivorous (insectivorous) plants. Kept under Animal Nutrition so placements already made stay valid. Sorting rule: how an organism obtains its food, or which group of organisms feeds in a stated way, goes here; an organism's place in a food chain as producer, consumer or decomposer goes to energy-flow.producers-consumers; naming an organism as an endoparasite or ectoparasite, or its effect on its host, goes to associations.parasitism; insectivorous plants go here, not under plant-nutrition.minerals.

subtopics.name: The alimentary system
subtopics.covers: Organs of the gut and associated glands, their structure, and what happens in each region. Sorting rule: a question about an organ's structure or role goes here; where the digestion of a named food begins, or an enzyme's action, goes under enzymes, even on a gut diagram.

subtopics.name: Teeth and dental formula
subtopics.covers: Types of teeth, their structure and functions, and dental formulae of herbivores, carnivores and humans.

subtopics.name: Feeding mechanisms
subtopics.covers: How protozoa, insects and mammals feed, and feeding habits.

topics.name: Ecosystems and Habitats
topics.syllabus: A.III.1, C habitats, JAMB C.1, JAMB C.3-4

subtopics.name: Components of an ecosystem and ecological terms
subtopics.syllabus: A.III.1, C ecological components, JAMB C.1
subtopics.covers: Biotic and abiotic components, the lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere, biotic factors such as food, predators and competitors as influences on where organisms live, and the terms population, community, habitat, niche, biosphere and ecosystem. Sorting rule: what a sealed or self-sustaining ecosystem, such as a balanced aquarium, needs goes here; the effect of a named physical factor goes to ecological-factors.physical; an organism's trophic role goes to energy-flow.producers-consumers.

subtopics.name: Habitats
subtopics.covers: Aquatic habitats (marine, estuarine, freshwater) and terrestrial habitats, including Nigeria's biomes (tropical rainforest, Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, Sahel and desert, montane highlands) with their climate, plants and animals, and the organisms typical of each. Sorting rule: which organisms and conditions characterise a habitat go here; how a factor such as salinity varies or affects life in a habitat goes to ecological-factors.physical.

topics.name: Ecological Factors
topics.syllabus: A.III.2-3, C ecological management, JAMB C.6

subtopics.name: Climatic, topographic and gaseous factors
subtopics.covers: Temperature, light, rainfall, humidity, wind, altitude, slope and gases, and in water salinity, turbidity and pH, and their effect on where organisms live. Sorting rule: how a factor varies, or what it does to organisms, goes here, even in a named habitat such as an estuary; the instrument used to measure it goes to ecological-factors.measurement; the range an organism tolerates goes to ecological-factors.tolerance; what a sealed aquarium needs goes to ecosystem.components.

subtopics.name: Soil (edaphic) factors
subtopics.covers: Soil composition, texture, water content, pH and air, and soil fertility: how it is lost (leaching, erosion, over-cropping, burning) and kept up or restored (crop rotation, manuring, fertilisers, contour ridging). Sorting rule: reading a soil condition from a plant's adaptation, such as pneumatophores, goes to adaptation.structural; how a practice changes soil fertility goes here; the wider ecological effects of a farming practice go to applied.agriculture.

subtopics.name: Measuring ecological factors
subtopics.covers: Instruments and methods for measuring temperature, humidity, light, turbidity, salinity, pH and rainfall, such as the Secchi disc, hygrometer and rain gauge. Sorting rule: the instrument or method goes here; how the factor varies goes to ecological-factors.physical.

subtopics.name: Tolerance and limiting range
subtopics.syllabus: C, ecological management, SoW SS1 T2 W3
subtopics.covers: The range of a factor within which an organism survives, its minimum, optimum and maximum, and a factor as limiting where an organism can live. Sorting rule: the range an organism tolerates goes here; what a named factor does in general goes to ecological-factors.physical; limiting factors of photosynthesis go to plant-nutrition.photosynthesis.

subtopics.name: Producers, consumers and decomposers
subtopics.covers: Autotrophs and heterotrophs, the trophic roles, and decomposition in nature. Sorting rule: an organism's trophic role goes here; how it obtains its food goes to animal-nutrition.modes; what a sealed aquarium needs goes to ecosystem.components.

subtopics.name: Food chains and food webs
subtopics.covers: Constructing and reading food chains and webs, and the effect of removing an organism.

subtopics.name: Ecological pyramids
subtopics.covers: Pyramids of numbers, biomass and energy: constructing them and explaining their shapes. Sorting rule: a question about a pyramid's shape or construction goes here; a question that uses the word biomass but asks only which organism is smallest goes to organisation.cell-forms.

subtopics.name: Energy transfer and loss
subtopics.covers: Energy transformation in nature (the sun as the source, light to chemical energy in photosynthesis, chemical energy to heat and work in respiration), how energy passes between trophic levels, and how much is lost at each step. Sorting rule: a question about the amount of energy transferred or lost, or the forms energy takes as it moves through an ecosystem, goes here, even if it mentions a pyramid; the steps of photosynthesis itself go to plant-nutrition.photosynthesis.

subtopics.name: Carbon cycle
subtopics.covers: Movement of carbon through photosynthesis, respiration, decay and combustion. Sorting rule: which process adds or removes carbon (IV) oxide from the atmosphere goes here, even when the answer is photosynthesis.

subtopics.name: Water cycle
subtopics.covers: Evaporation, transpiration, condensation and precipitation.

subtopics.name: Nitrogen cycle
subtopics.covers: Nitrogen fixation, nitrification, denitrification and the bacteria involved, including Rhizobium in root nodules. Sorting rule: nitrogen-fixing bacteria go here, not under microorganisms.useful; a question asking what kind of association a root nodule shows goes to associations.symbiosis.

subtopics.name: Symbiosis and types of association
subtopics.covers: Associations in which both organisms benefit (mutualism), and identifying which type of association a named pair shows: mutualism, commensalism, parasitism or saprophytism. Sorting rule: a question that names a pair, such as cattle and egret, and asks for the type of association goes here whatever the answer; questions about parasites themselves go to associations.parasitism.

subtopics.name: Parasites and their hosts
subtopics.covers: Associations in which one benefits and the other is harmed, or unaffected: parasites and commensals, endoparasites and ectoparasites, their adaptations and their effects on the host. Sorting rule: naming an organism as a parasite, endoparasite or ectoparasite, or saying what it does to its host, goes here, including a single-celled parasite such as Plasmodium; which type of association a named pair shows goes to associations.symbiosis; parasitic nutrition named as a mode goes to animal-nutrition.modes.

subtopics.name: Competition and predation
subtopics.covers: Factors that bring about competition, intra and inter-species competition, and predator and prey. Sorting rule: the effects of overcrowding on one population go to population.growth; competition as a driver of succession goes to population.succession.

topics.name: Population Ecology
topics.syllabus: A.III.7, C population studies, C balance in nature

subtopics.name: Population size and growth
subtopics.covers: Factors that change population size, growth curves and carrying capacity, the effects of overcrowding, and balance in nature, the dynamic equilibrium of populations. Sorting rule: a question about why a population changes, or what overcrowding does to it, goes here, even when the answer is competition.

subtopics.name: Ecological succession
subtopics.covers: Primary and secondary succession, pioneer species, dominance and climax communities, and how competition drives succession. Sorting rule: competition as the cause of one community replacing another goes here; types of competition in general go to associations.competition.

subtopics.name: Estimating population size
subtopics.covers: Quadrats, transects, capture and recapture, density, frequency and abundance. Sorting rule: a question about how a population is counted or measured goes here.

topics.name: Microorganisms and Health
topics.syllabus: A.III.8, C microorganisms, C public health, JAMB C.7

subtopics.name: Microorganisms around us
subtopics.covers: Bacteria, viruses, fungi and protozoa, their structure and where they are found. Sorting rule: the structure, shapes and habitats of bacteria go here; a feature that places bacteria in Monera, or a prokaryote and eukaryote comparison, goes to classification.kingdoms.

subtopics.name: Culturing microorganisms
subtopics.covers: Preparing culture media, sterilising, inoculating and incubating, and measuring the growth of a culture by colony counts or turbidity. Sorting rule: technique for growing and measuring a culture goes here; general handling of apparatus goes to practical.lab; killing microorganisms to prevent disease goes to microorganisms.disease.

subtopics.name: Disease, its transmission and control
subtopics.covers: How diseases spread, carriers and vectors, common diseases, and controlling harmful microorganisms by heat, chemicals and ultraviolet light. Sorting rule: how a disease spreads, or how it or its vector is controlled, goes here; refuse, sewage, sanitation, food hygiene and health organisations go to microorganisms.public-health; methods of keeping food from spoiling go to applied.food-preservation.

subtopics.name: Public health and sanitation
subtopics.syllabus: A.III.8(d)(i), C public health, JAMB C.7(b)(ii)
subtopics.covers: Refuse and sewage disposal, sanitation, safe water, food hygiene, and the work of health organisations such as the WHO and local health services. Sorting rule: disposal methods and their health purpose go here; sewage's effect on the life of a river goes to conservation.pollution; how a named disease spreads goes to microorganisms.disease.

subtopics.name: Immunity and vaccination
subtopics.covers: Natural and artificial immunity, antibodies, and vaccines. Sorting rule: agglutination in a blood transfusion goes to variation.applications.

subtopics.name: Useful microorganisms
subtopics.covers: Microorganisms in food production, industry and decay. Sorting rule: nitrogen-fixing bacteria go to nutrient-cycles.nitrogen; growing and measuring a culture goes to microorganisms.culturing.

subtopics.name: Resources to be conserved
subtopics.covers: The meaning of conservation, as against preservation and use; soil, water, wildlife, forests and minerals as resources, renewable and non-renewable; and endangered and extinct species. Sorting rule: what conservation means, or which species are endangered, goes here; how resources are conserved goes to conservation.methods.

subtopics.name: Ways of ensuring conservation
subtopics.covers: Reserves, national parks, laws, afforestation, recycling and conservation agencies. Sorting rule: the meaning of conservation goes to conservation.resources.

subtopics.name: Pollution
subtopics.covers: Pollution of air, water and soil, its sources and effects, and noise. The syllabus places this under ecological management. Sorting rule: a pollutant's effect on living things goes here; methods of disposing of refuse and sewage go to microorganisms.public-health; the wider effects of a named farming practice go to applied.agriculture.

subtopics.name: Continuous and discontinuous variation
subtopics.covers: Variation that grades smoothly (height, weight) against variation in distinct classes (blood group, tongue rolling). Added after 2025 Q41 fell across two subtopics. Sorting rule: what causes a trait, inherited or environmental, goes to variation.causes.

subtopics.name: Causes of variation: inherited and environmental
subtopics.covers: Whether a trait comes from genes, from the environment (acquired characters), or from both, and why individuals with the same genes can differ. Tested in WAEC 2016 Q41. Sorting rule: what causes a trait or a difference goes here; whether it is continuous or discontinuous goes to variation.types; Lamarck's inheritance of acquired characters as a theory goes to evolution.theories.

subtopics.name: Morphological variation
subtopics.covers: Differences in visible features: height, colour, fingerprints, shape. Sorting rule: when a question asks whether a trait is continuous or discontinuous, use variation.types.

subtopics.name: Physiological variation
subtopics.covers: Differences in body function: tongue rolling, tasting, blood group. Sorting rule: a blood group question goes here only when it asks what kind of variation a blood group is; transfusion goes to variation.applications and inheritance to genetics.applications.

subtopics.name: Uses of variation: crime detection, transfusion, paternity
subtopics.covers: Fingerprints and blood groups used in crime detection, blood transfusion and paternity. Sorting rule for blood groups: donor and recipient compatibility, universal donor and recipient, and agglutination after transfusion go here; any question answered by a genetic cross, including a paternity cross, goes to genetics.applications; a blood group named as an example of variation goes to variation.physiological.

subtopics.name: Genetic terminology
subtopics.covers: Gene, allele, genotype, phenotype, dominant, recessive, homozygous and heterozygous, and mutation defined, with gene and chromosome mutation as its kinds. Sorting rule: what a mutation is goes here; a mutation's effects in genetic disorders and breeding go to genetics.applications.

subtopics.name: Mendel's laws, crosses and ratios
subtopics.covers: Mendel's laws, monohybrid crosses, Punnett squares, and the ratios and probabilities they give. Probability was merged here: the syllabus does not require probability as a separate calculation, and every cross ends in one.

subtopics.name: Chromosomes, DNA and replication
subtopics.covers: Chromosome structure, the chromosome number of a named species, genes on chromosomes, DNA and RNA structure, their bases and base pairing, and DNA replication. Tested in 2025 Q45 and Q46. Sorting rule: crossing over, and haploid and diploid numbers in gametes and zygotes, go to cell.division.

subtopics.name: Sex determination, linkage and sex-linked traits
subtopics.covers: How sex is determined, linkage, and sex-linked traits such as haemophilia and colour blindness.

subtopics.name: Applications of heredity
subtopics.covers: Heredity in agriculture and medicine, genetic disorders, the effects of mutation, and blood group inheritance. Sorting rule: what a mutation is goes to genetics.terminology. For blood groups, any question answered by a genetic cross, including a paternity cross, goes here; transfusion compatibility and agglutination go to variation.applications; a blood group named as an example of variation goes to variation.physiological.

subtopics.name: Behavioural adaptation
subtopics.covers: Behaviour that helps an animal survive: social organisation and castes in termites, bees and ants, migration, hibernation, aestivation, basking and territoriality. Sorting rule: courtship and display behaviour, such as the lizard's gular fold, goes to reproduction.animals-compared; a body structure goes to adaptation.structural.

subtopics.name: Structural adaptation
subtopics.covers: Structures adapted for obtaining food, locomotion, protection, securing mates and surviving harsh conditions, and reading a habitat or soil condition from an adaptation, such as pneumatophores showing waterlogged soil. Sorting rule: a body structure goes here; a display behaviour goes to reproduction.animals-compared; soil properties asked for their own sake go to ecological-factors.edaphic.

subtopics.name: Adaptive colouration
subtopics.covers: Camouflage, warning colouration and mimicry.

subtopics.name: Evidence of evolution
subtopics.covers: Fossils, comparative anatomy, embryology, geographical distribution, and genetic studies.

subtopics.name: Theories of evolution and natural selection
subtopics.covers: Lamarck's use and disuse and inheritance of acquired characters, Darwin's natural selection, the role of mutation, and speciation. Natural selection was merged here because Darwin's theory is natural selection. Sorting rule: ordering groups by advancement goes to evolution.trends.

subtopics.name: Evolutionary trends across groups
subtopics.covers: The order of groups from simple to complex and primitive to advanced, such as algae, mosses, ferns, conifers and flowering plants, or Hydra to mammals, and which group is most primitive. Tested in UTME 2021 Q23 and 2025 Q9 and WAEC 2022 Q50. Sorting rule: ordering groups or picking the most primitive goes here, not under classification.kingdoms, organisation.complexity or evolution.theories; the features that place an organism in a group go to classification.kingdoms.

subtopics.name: Biology as a science
subtopics.covers: What biology is, its branches (botany, zoology, microbiology and others) and specialised fields, its importance in everyday life, and biology-related careers. Sorting rule: the scientific method and report writing go to practical.experiments.

subtopics.name: Laboratory techniques and safety
subtopics.covers: Handling apparatus and specimens, preserving, and laboratory safety. Sorting rule: growing and measuring a culture of microorganisms goes to microorganisms.culturing.

subtopics.name: The microscope
subtopics.covers: Parts of the microscope, how to use it, and magnification.

subtopics.name: Symmetry, sectioning and orientation
subtopics.covers: Radial and bilateral symmetry, longitudinal, transverse and vertical sections, and orientation terms such as anterior, posterior, dorsal and ventral. Sorting rule: how to draw and label a section goes to practical.drawing; which group of animals shows a kind of symmetry goes to classification.kingdoms.

subtopics.name: Biological drawing
subtopics.covers: Rules of biological drawing, labelling and magnification of a drawing.

subtopics.name: Experiments and data handling
subtopics.covers: Experimental design, controls, reading tables and graphs, and drawing conclusions.

topics.name: Biology in Agriculture and Industry
topics.syllabus: C relevance to agriculture, C.7(e), B biology and industry

subtopics.name: Classifying plants by life span
subtopics.syllabus: C, relevance of biology to agriculture (a)
subtopics.covers: Annuals, biennials and perennials. Split out after 2025 Q20 was hidden inside a broad agriculture label.

subtopics.name: Biology and agriculture
subtopics.syllabus: C, relevance of biology to agriculture, C.7(f)
subtopics.covers: Crop improvement, pests and their control, including the life histories of pests such as weevils and cotton stainers, farming practices, and the effects of practices such as bush burning, tillage, fertilisers and herbicides on the ecosystem. Sorting rule: how a practice changes soil fertility goes to ecological-factors.edaphic; general sources of pollution go to conservation.pollution; methods of storing and preserving food go to applied.food-preservation.

subtopics.name: Food preservation and storage
subtopics.covers: Drying, salting, smoking, cooling and freezing, canning and chemical preservatives, how each stops spoilage, and storing food and grain. Sorting rule: keeping food from spoiling goes here; hygiene in handling food goes to microorganisms.public-health; the life history and control of a storage pest such as the weevil go to applied.agriculture.

subtopics.name: Biotechnology
subtopics.covers: Genetic engineering, recombinant DNA, and applied uses of microorganisms.

legacy_note: Each of the 106 legacy database topics is folded into a subtopic where its name is specific, or into a parent topic where it is generic. A question moved to a parent is correct but unplaced within it, and is flagged for reclassification rather than guessed into a subtopic. In version 2.2, Homeostasis and Plant morphology and anatomy moved to the new subtopics that now match their names.

v1_to_v2.symbiosis-adaptation: SPLIT: associations (ecology) or adaptation (evolution), decided per question
v1_to_v2.variation-evolution: SPLIT: variation or evolution, decided per question
